title: Random Point in View: Fair Sample Points
description: Use Random Point in View to generate random points inside your map view or study area — for sampling, games and unbiased spot checks. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a soil researcher frames the study field, generates 20 random points, and the sampling stops following the footpaths and starts following the statistics.
quick_answer: Random Point in View generates random points inside the map area you frame — for sampling designs, games, drills and unbiased spot checks. Pan and zoom to your study area, choose how many points you need, and generate a set whose only pattern is that it has none.
steps_intro: Randomness with a boundary — you supply the frame, chance supplies the points:

body.t: Soil cores, vegetation quadrats, litter counts: human-chosen 'random' spots cluster near paths and gates. Generated points inside the study frame remove the researcher's feet from the design. Bound the area first in the
Geocaching-style challenges, photo-a-day prompts, 'visit a random point in our county' — the generator deals the destination fairly.
Random inspection points for assets spread over an area: the fairest inspection is the one nobody could predict or lobby. Mark the chosen few with the
Generate 10 points, then 1,000, and watch clumping appear in both — real randomness clusters, and seeing it cures the 'evenly spread' misconception better than any lecture.

A student's 15 'random' hand-picked soil spots all sat within 20 paces of the field path. Fifteen generated points sent her to the far corners — and the nitrogen results changed enough to rewrite the conclusion.

Frame the whole world and generate: about 71% of points land in ocean, because about 71% of Earth's surface is ocean. Random-on-a-map is honest about the planet's proportions whether you wanted the lesson or not.

popular_table.intro: Rules of thumb — real designs deserve a statistician, practice runs deserve these.
rows: Enough to see clumping and gaps
popular_table.note: Points are drawn uniformly across the framed view's rectangle of latitude and longitude. At neighbourhood scale that is effectively uniform on the ground; at world scale, equal longitude bands squeeze toward the poles, so frame tightly around your real study area.

faq: A fresh generate deals a fresh set — that is the point of random. If a set matters (an audit, a published design), export or pin the points immediately; the dealt hand is only kept if you keep it.
Can I restrict points to land only?

Frame the view tightly around your land area to make water points rare; a true land-mask filter is a GIS feature. Treat a stray water point as a redraw, and say so in your method notes if it is research.
Can points fall outside my study plot?
Points fill the framed view, so frame the view to the plot. For an irregular boundary, generate generously and discard outsiders — discarding by a rule written in advance keeps the design honest.
Is uniform-in-view the same as uniform-on-ground?
At local scales, yes for practical purposes. Across continents, longitude lines converge, so view-uniform points over-sample high latitudes per square kilometre — one more reason to frame tightly.
How do I navigate to a generated point?
Copy its coordinates into any map app, or pin it here and share the view. In the field, your phone's GPS and the point's coordinates are the whole system.
Can I generate points along a line or in a ring?
This generator fills an area. Rings and transects are structured designs — build them with the Coordinate Radius Points Generator or by drawing in the Map Drawer.
What about random points for a whole country?

Frame the country and generate plenty, discarding sea and border overshoot. For regular official sampling frames, national statistics offices publish grids — this tool is the fast, honest approximation.
Because randomness clusters. Uniform points are not evenly-spaced points; if your design needs even coverage, that is a grid or stratified design — a different, also respectable, tool choice.
